title: Queratina para el cabello: usos, riesgos y alternativas
summary: Tu cabello se ve opaco, quebradizo, con frizz imposible de controlar. Lo probaste todo —aceites, mascarillas, cambios de champú— y nada funciona. En la peluquería te dicen "queratina" como si fuera la respuesta mágica a todos tus problemas capilares. La queratina para el cabello
body_text: Tu cabello se ve opaco, quebradizo, con frizz imposible de controlar. Lo probaste todo —aceites, mascarillas, cambios de champú— y nada funciona. En la peluquería te dicen "queratina" como si fuera la respuesta mágica a todos tus problemas capilares. Pero antes de gastar $200.000 en un tratamiento de queratina, conviene entender qué hace realmente, qué riesgos esconde y —sobre todo— si tu problema de cabello es realmente un problema de queratina o algo más profundo. La queratina para el cabello es uno de los tratamientos de estética más populares en Chile y América Latina. Pero la ciencia detrás de estos tratamientos es más compleja de lo que la publicidad reconoce, y en algunos casos pueden hacer más daño que bien. ¿Qué es la queratina y por qué tu cabello la necesita? La queratina es una proteína estructural que compone naturalmente tu cabello, tus uñas y la capa externa de tu piel. Es como los ladrillos que forman la pared de cada hebra capilar: le dan resistencia, elasticidad y brillo. Un cabello sano contiene aproximadamente un 95% de queratina. Cuando el cabello se daña —por calor, químicos, sol, o desnutrición— esa capa de queratina se rompe. Las cutículas se abren, el cabello pierde su estructura y aparecen los síntomas que conoces: frizz, resequedad, puntas abiertas, pérdida de brillo. El razonamiento de los tratamientos de queratina es simple: si tu cabello perdió queratina, reponerla debería arreglarlo. ¿Pero funciona así de simple? No exactamente. Y entender por qué es clave antes de tomar cualquier decisión. Tipos de tratamientos de queratina: cuál es cuál Existe mucha confusión sobre qué es exactamente un "tratamiento de queratina". Bajo ese paraguas se agrupan procedimientos muy diferentes, con distintos mecanismos de acción, precios y niveles de riesgo. Aquí van los principales: Alisado brasileño (Brazilian Blowout) Es el tratamiento de queratina más conocido y popular. Consiste en aplicar un producto a base de queratina (y, tradicionalmente, formaldehído) sobre el cabello húmedo, sellarlo con plancha a alta temperatura (230°C) y dejarlo actuar. El resultado es un cabello liso, brillante y sin frizz durante 3-5 meses. El problema histórico: el formaldehído se usa para fijar la queratina al cabello, y su liberación durante el planchado genera gases tóxicos que pueden causar irritación respiratoria, reacciones alérgicas y —según la Agencia Internacional para la Investigación del Cáncer (IARC)— es un carcinógeno conocido. Alisado japonés (thermal reconditioning) Es un proceso químico permanente que reestructura los enlaces del cabello usando hidróxido de sodio o guanidina. No utiliza queratina como ingrediente activo, aunque algunos salones la añaden como tratamiento posterior. Produce un alisado permanente (hasta que crece cabello nuevo), pero es agresivo y no se recomienda para cabello ya dañado. Tratamiento de queratina sin formol Versiones más recientes reemplazan el formaldehído por alternativas como el ácido glioxílico o cisteína. Suelen ser menos duraderas (6-8 semanas) y el resultado no es tan dramático, pero evitan la exposición al formol. Sin embargo , estudios han demostrado que algunos productos etiquetados como "libre de formaldehído" siguen liberando formaldehído cuando se calientan con la plancha. Tabla comparativa: tratamientos de queratina en Chile Tratamiento Precio aprox. (CLP) Duración Nivel de riesgo ¿Usa formol? Alisado brasileño tradicional $80.000 - $250.000 3-5 meses Alto Sí (o sus precursores) Queratina sin formol $60.000 - $180.000 6-8 semanas Moderado No declarado, pero puede liberar Alisado japonés $150.000 - $300.000+ Permanente (hasta crecimiento) Alto No, pero usa otros químicos agresivos Botox capilar (queratina + vitaminas) $50.000 - $120.000 4-8 semanas Bajo-Moderado Generalmente no Mascarillas de queratina (uso doméstico) $5.000 - $25.000 Efímero (1-2 lavados) Muy bajo No ¿Sientes que tu cabello no responde a ningún tratamiento? El problema podría no estar en la queratina sino en una deficiencia nutricional. Un examen de sangre para caída del cabello puede revelar si falta hierro, tiroides desregulada o déficit vitamínico. Antes de gastar en la peluquería, descarta que el problema venga de adentro. ¿El tratamiento de queratina realmente funciona? Qué dice la ciencia La respuesta corta: sí, pero temporalmente y con matices. Los tratamientos de queratina funcionan de dos formas. Primero, la queratina aplicada rellena temporalmente los espacios dañados en la cutícula capilar, lo que da la sensación de cabello más liso y brillante. Segundo, el calor de la plancha funde y sella esta capa, creando un efecto protector externo. Pero la ciencia es clara en un punto: la queratina aplicada tópicamente no penetra al interior del cabello de forma permanente . Es un tratamiento cosmético superficial, no una reparación estructural. Un estudio publicado en el International Journal of Trichology evaluó multiple productos comerciales de queratina y encontró que el efecto reparador se pierde progresivamente con cada lavado, sin mejorar la integridad estructural subyacente del cabello. Esto significa que si tu cabello está dañado por una causa subyacente —desnutrición, déficit de hierro, problemas tiroideos—, la queratina va a maquillarlo temporalmente sin resolver el problema real. Es como pintar sobre un muro con humedad: se ve bien por un tiempo, pero el daño sigue ahí debajo. El problema del formaldehído: el riesgo oculto de la "queratina sin formol" Este es probablemente el aspecto más importante de este artículo, y muchas salones no lo explican con claridad. El formaldehído es lo que hace que el alisado brasileño tradicional funcione tan bien. Es el agente químico que "fija" la queratina al cabello, creando enlaces cruzados entre las proteínas. Sin formaldehído (o sin un químico que cumpla una función similar), el tratamiento es mucho menos efectivo y duradero. El problema es que el formaldehído es tóxico . La Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos de EE.UU. (FDA) ha emitido múltiples advertencias sobre productos para el alisado del cabello que contienen formaldehído o sus precursores, señalando riesgos que incluyen: Irritación de ojos, nariz y garganta Reacciones alérgicas en piel y cuero cabelludo Dificultad para respirar y tos durante y después del tratamiento Riesgo de cáncer con exposición repetida (clasificado como carcinógeno humano Grupo 1 por la IARC) ¿"Libre de formol" significa realmente libre? No siempre. Un estudio de 2020 publicado en la revista Contact Dermatitis analizó productos etiquetados como "formaldehyde-free" y encontró que muchos contenían precursores del formaldehído —sustancias como metileno glicol o hemiformal— que liberan formaldehído cuando se calientan con la plancha. Legalmente, el producto "no contiene formaldehído" en su formulación, pero durante el tratamiento, el cliente y el estilista sí lo inhalan. La advertencia es simple: desconfía del "sin formol" sin certificación de laboratorio independiente . Si el tratamiento requiere plancha a más de 200°C sobre el producto aplicado, hay riesgo de liberación de formaldehído. Queratina natural: ¿puedes mejorar tu cabello desde adentro? Si la queratina es una proteína que tu cuerpo produce naturalmente, ¿se puede estimular esa producción con nutrición? La respuesta es sí, parcialmente. Tu cuerpo sintetiza queratina a partir de aminoácidos —los bloques constructores de las proteínas— que obtienes de la alimentación. No puedes "comer queratina" directamente para enviarla al cabello (la queratina dietaria se descompone en aminoácidos durante la digestión), pero sí puedes asegurar que tu cuerpo tenga todos los nutrientes necesarios para producirla de forma eficiente. Los nutrientes clave para la producción natural de queratina capilar incluyen: Proteína de alta calidad: huevos, pescado, pollo, legumbres. Sin aminoácidos suficientes (especialmente cisteína y metionina), el cuerpo no puede producir queratina. Es el primer punto a revisitar. Biotina (vitamina B7): fundamental para el metabolismo de los aminoácidos que forman queratina. La deficiencia de biotina causa fragilidad capilar. Puedes profundizar en esto en nuestra guía sobre biotina para el cabello . Zinc: el zinc es necesario para la división celular en el folículo piloso. Su deficiencia es una causa directa de caída y fragilidad del cabello. Vitamina A: en cantidades adecuadas, ayuda a las glándulas sebáceas a producir sebo, que hidrata el cabello naturalmente. En exceso, paradójicamente, causa caída. Silicio: un mineral menos conocido pero con evidencia creciente. Estudios sugieren que mejora la elasticidad y resistencia del cabello. Hierro: la deficiencia de hierro es una de las causas más subdiagnosticadas de daño capilar en mujeres, especialmente en edad reproductiva. Lee más sobre hierro bajo y caída del cabello . Para una guía completa de qué comer, revisa nuestro artículo sobre alimentos para fortalecer el cabello . Cuando el daño capilar NO es un problema de queratina Aquí está el punto crítico que muchos salones no consideran: si tu cabello está opaco, quebradizo o se cae, el problema puede no estar en el cabello en absoluto . Puede estar en tu cuerpo. Estas son las causas más comunes de daño capilar que se confunden con "falta de queratina": Deficiencia de hierro y ferritina baja La ferropenia es una de las causas más frecuentes de caída y fragilidad capilar en mujeres chilenas en edad menstruante. Los síntomas —cabello fino, quebradizo, con pérdida de volumen— son casi idénticos a los del "daño por queratina". Si tu ferritina está baja, ningún tratamiento tópico de queratina va a resolver el problema. Problemas de tiroides Tanto el hipotiroidismo como el hipertiroidismo causan cambios significativos en la textura y salud del cabello. El cabello se vuelve seco, áspero y tiende a caerse. Es un síntoma clásico que muchas mujeres atribuyen a "estrés" o "cabello dañado" cuando la causa real está en la tiroides y la caída del cabello . Estrés crónico y efluvio telógeno El estrés físico o emocional intenso puede empujar a los folículos pilosos a una fase de reposo, causando una caída difusa 2-3 meses después del evento desencadenante. Esto se llama efluvio telógeno , y no tiene nada que ver con la queratina. Si estás perdiendo cabello de forma difusa, lee sobre la caída del cabello por estrés . Deficiencia de vitamina D La vitamina D está involucrada en la creación de nuevos folículos pilosos. Su deficiencia se asocia con caída del cabello y reducción en su grosor. Caida del cabello por otras causas La lista es larga: cambios hormonales postparto, medicamentos, caída del cabello en mujeres por causas genéticas, uso prolongado de tratamientos químicos previos. Si quieres explorar alternativas, algunas personas consideran el aceite de romero para el cabello o tratamientos médicos como minoxidil o plasma rico en plaquetas . Antes de invertir en un tratamiento de queratina, asegúrate de que el problema no esté dentro de tu cuerpo. Un examen de sangre para caída del cabello evalúa hierro, tiroides, vitaminas y más — todo desde la comodidad de tu casa. En Examedi hacemos exámenes de sangre a domicilio en Santiago y otras regiones de Chile. Pide tu examen a domicilio → ¿El tratamiento de queratina daña el cabello a largo plazo? Esta es la pregunta que nadie en la peluquería quiere responder con honestidad. Y la respuesta es: depende del tipo de tratamiento y de la condición previa de tu cabello. El mecanismo del tratamiento de queratina implica planchar el cabello a temperaturas de 200-230°C con el producto aplicado. Ese calor extremo, por sí solo, causa daño estructural a la cutícula capilar. Cada sesión somete al cabello a un estrés térmico que, acumulado, puede producir exactamente el efecto contrario al deseado: cabello más quebradizo, más opaco y con mayor tendencia a romperse. Un estudio publicado en el Journal of Cosmetic Science demostró que los tratamientos térmicos repetidos sobre cabello tratado con queratina causan degradación progresiva de la corteza capilar, resultando en pérdida de elasticidad que no se recupera con tratamientos posteriores. Además, los tratamientos que contienen formaldehído pueden causar: Endurecimiento del tallo capilar: el cabello se ve liso pero pierde elasticidad, volviéndose más propenso a romperse. Sequedad del cuero cabelludo: algunos productos irritan el cuero cabelludo, lo que puede empeorar la salud del folículo. Dependencia cosmética: al desgastarse el efecto (6-8 semanas), el cabello puede verse peor que antes del tratamiento, llevando a repetir el ciclo. La conclusión de los dermatólogos trichólogos: los tratamientos de queratina no son inherentemente destructivos si se hacen de forma ocasional y con productos de calidad, pero no deben usarse como solución permanente a un problema capilar subyacente. Preguntas frecuentes ¿Cuánto dura el tratamiento de queratina en el cabello? La duración depende del tipo de tratamiento. Un alisado brasileño tradicional dura entre 3 y 5 meses. Los tratamientos sin formol suelen durar 6 a 8 semanas. El alisado japonés es permanente hasta que crece cabello nuevo, pero requiere retoques en la raíz cada 4-6 meses. La duración también depende del cuidado posterior: usar champús sin sulfatos, evitar lavados muy frecuentes y minimizar el calor prolongan el efecto. ¿Puedo hacerme un tratamiento de queratina si estoy embarazada? La mayoría de los dermatólogos recomiendan no realizarse tratamientos de queratina durante el embarazo, especialmente aquellos que usan formaldehído o sus precursores. Los vapores químicos pueden ser perjudiciales y el cuero cabelludo es más sensible durante la gestación. Si estás embarazada y tu cabello se ve dañado, revisa primero si hay una causa nutricional: el embarazo aumenta la demanda de hierro y otros nutrientes. ¿La queratina sirve para la caída del cabello? No. Los tratamientos de queratina actúan sobre el tallo capilar —la parte visible del cabello— mejorando su apariencia externa. No tienen ningún efecto sobre el folículo piloso, que es donde se origina la caída. Si tu problema es que el cabello se cae, la queratina no es la solución. Necesitas identificar la causa de la caída, que puede ser hormonal, nutricional o genética. El trasplante capilar en Chile es una opción para casos avanzados. ¿Cada cuánto se puede repetir el tratamiento de queratina? Lo recomendable es esperar al menos 3 meses entre tratamientos, y no exceder 2-3 por año. Dar tiempo al cabello para que se recupere del estrés térmico es fundamental. Si sientes que necesitas repetir el tratamiento cada mes, es probable que el problema original no se haya resuelto y debas revisar la salud interna de tu cabello. ¿Qué alternativas naturales existen a la queratina? No existe una "queratina natural" tópica que replique el efecto del tratamiento químico, pero puedes mejorar la salud de tu cabello cuidando los nutrientes que tu cuerpo necesita para producir queratina naturalmente: suficientes proteínas, biotina, zinc, hierro y vitaminas A y D. También puedes usar mascarillas capilares con proteínas hidrolizadas que ofrecen un efecto similar, aunque mucho más sutil y temporal. ¿El tratamiento de queratina causa cáncer? El tratamiento en sí no está clasificado como carcinogénico, pero la exposición al formaldehído que se libera durante el procedimiento sí es una preocupación de salud pública. La IARC clasifica el formaldehído como carcinógeno humano Grupo 1. La exposición ocasional en un salón bien ventilado probablemente no represente un riesgo significativo, pero los estilistas que realizan estos tratamientos diariamente sí tienen mayor riesgo. title: Rio Tinto releases second quarter 2026 production results
body_text: Driving performance to achieve 3% YoY CuEq1 growth in the first half MELBOURNE, Australia--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Rio Tinto Chief Executive Simon Trott said: "We are delivering growth as we drive performance across the group, with copper equivalent production up 3 per cent in the first half. “Our scale, geographical diversification and sophisticated supply chains continue to underpin our resilience and strong operational performance despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainty throughout the period. “In the Pilbara, we achieved our highest first half iron ore production since we set a record in 2018, through the successful implementation of our ongoing productivity improvement program. In copper, Oyu Tolgoi continued to ramp up on schedule to deliver more than 30 per cent growth for the first half, while our integrated, large-scale aluminium business sustained its strong performance. “At Simandou, we continue to advance at pace. SimFer mine construction and port infrastructure are both now more than three quarters complete, with full rail commissioning achieved in the first quarter. We are progressing our next generation of copper growth options at Resolution and Winu, while in lithium we achieved first production ahead of plan at Sal de Vida and Fénix 1B. “We are driving a step-change in operational performance to deliver industry leading returns and growth for our shareholders." Executive Summary Operational excellence: 3% YoY increase in copper equivalent (CuEq)1 production for the first half. Copper: Oyu Tolgoi ramp-up remains on track; H1 production delivered 31% YoY growth. Copper C1 net unit cost guidance has been reduced to US 30 - 50c/lb (from US 65 - 75c/lb). Iron ore: Q2 global iron ore sales were 89Mt, up 5% YoY. Q2 Pilbara sales up 7% YoY. SimFer mine construction and port infrastructure now both over three quarters complete. Aluminium: Resilience across the supply chain, with a strong recovery in bauxite. Lithium: Production rose 20% YoY in Q2 driven by the ramp-up at Rincon starter plant and delivery of first tonnes at Sal de Vida and Fénix 1B, ahead of plan. title: AI for Recruitment Efficiency: 10 Ways to Streamline Your Hiring Process
summary: Discover how AI automates 80% of recruiting tasks. Learn 10 proven ways to reduce admin burden, scale interviews 24/7, and boost recruiter productivity with Alex.
body_text: Your recruiters spend the majority of their time on administrative tasks: scheduling interviews, updating your Applicant Tracking System (ATS), and chasing responses. Alex transforms this reality by automating these workflows, freeing your team for strategic work that closes placements. Here's what you'll learn in this article: How AI eliminates resume screening bottlenecks and surfaces qualified candidates from hundreds of applications Why structured interviews deliver 23% better reliability than unstructured processes How automated workflows free recruiters from administrative tasks to focus on strategic hiring How Verify protects hiring integrity against modern candidate fraud How to rediscover silver-medalist candidates already in your ATS before spending on job boards These strategies work together to help recruiting teams achieve the 80/20 flip: moving from 80% admin work to 80% strategic, revenue-generating activities. 1. Eliminate Resume Screening Bottlenecks When applications flood in by the hundreds, recruiters face an impossible choice: spend hours reviewing every resume or risk missing qualified candidates entirely. Manual screening creates operational bottlenecks that slow time-to-hire and frustrate hiring managers waiting for qualified shortlists. Resume Screens evaluates every incoming application with transparent scoring and structured rationale, so recruiters know exactly why a candidate was recommended or flagged. For candidates who advance, AI Interviews conducts structured conversations with every candidate rather than requiring manual phone screens. The platform conducts 5,000+ interviews daily, ensuring 100% candidate coverage with consistent evaluation. Organizations implementing AI-powered recruitment screening report significant cost-per-hire reductions and time-to-hire improvements by eliminating the manual screening bottleneck entirely. title: AI Spatial Assist makes BIM accessible to every construction stakeholder
body_text: Today we're excited to announce the launch of AI Spatial Assist , a new AI capability that allows anyone, regardless of BIM expertise, to instantly navigate, interrogate, and review complex building models using natural language. Available across Resolve's high-performance web viewer and immersive VR environment, AI Spatial Assist enables teams to ask questions, locate equipment, teleport to rooms, and navigate models in seconds without relying on technical specialists or complex software interfaces. The launch addresses one of construction's most persistent productivity drains: the time it takes to find and validate project information. Industry research shows project teams spend roughly 20% of the time in meetings or long communication threads and another 14% tracking down information each week. A significant portion of that time is spent doing model reviews, scheduling coordination sessions, screen-sharing navigation, and relying on BIM specialists to retrieve answers locked inside complex 3D environments. Yet despite this massive coordination investment, many projects still suffer costly downstream rework. When operability constraints, installation conflicts, or access issues go unnoticed during design, they surface later during procurement, installation, or commissioning. And at a time where the demands for AI infrastructure are higher than ever, the industry cannot afford these delays. Eliminating the BIM Bottleneck Historically, BIM review has depended on BIM/VDC specialists to operate software, navigate geometry, and extract insights. This created an operational bottleneck where subject matter experts, from facilities leaders to field teams, can't easily validate design models on their own. AI Spatial Assist removes that dependency and frees up VDC teams for higher impact work. Users can simply ask: "Take me to the electrical room on Level 2." "Where are the cooling towers located?" "Which P&ID is this valve a part of?" The AI agent understands BIM geometry and metadata for seamless navigation and understanding of complex 3D models. If you've clicked on an object in the model, the agent will also use that context to answer questions like "what is this?" Improving Speed and Quality at the Same Time AI Spatial Assist is designed to improve both delivery velocity and quality simultaneously. By making BIM instantly accessible, the platform eliminates meetings whose sole purpose is navigating models or retrieving information. Subject matter experts can review directly, validate assumptions earlier, and flag risks without waiting on technical intermediaries. At the same time, broader participation leads to better outcomes. Facilities teams validate maintainability. Field leaders assess install risks. Operators confirm equipment access and safety, all before construction begins. Feedback cycles are compressed from weeks to minutes and deliverables are better aligned with the realities of construction and operations. Capturing What Rules-Based AI Misses Many emerging AI tools in design and construction focus on rules-based validation by checking models against documented requirements such as permitting regulations, building codes, and engineering standards. While critical, these systems operate on knowledge that is already written down. Some of construction's highest-value intelligence, however, is rarely formally documented. Operational feedback about maintainability, service access, installation practicality, and real-world usability lives primarily in the experience of facilities leaders, operators, and field teams. Historically, this expertise has been difficult to capture, easy to lose between projects, and rarely incorporated upstream into design. As the industry faces a growing labor shortage and generational workforce transition, preserving and scaling this knowledge is becoming increasingly urgent. By making BIM models instantly accessible through natural language, AI Spatial Assist enables these stakeholders to engage directly allowing teams to capture and structure feedback that would otherwise remain siloed or lost. The First Step Toward Compounding Intelligence Resolve positions AI Spatial Assist as the foundation of a broader vision. One where every project review strengthens the next. Each interaction generates structured insight: risks identified, access issues flagged, coordination conflicts surfaced, and operational feedback captured. Over time, this creates a growing intelligence layer across infrastructure portfolios. Resolve AI Spatial Assist is rolling out to select partners today and teams can sign up for the waitlist at https://www.resolvebim.com/ai

title: Duvet vs. Comforter: What Is a Duvet + Key Differences
summary: Discover the differences between a duvet and a comforter. Learn how each type of blanket works plus how to choose the right option for you.
body_text: Key Takeaways A duvet is a type of blanket utilizing a multi-layered fabric filled with stuffing made from natural or synthetic fibers. Duvet inserts go into a duvet cover for added warmth, comfort, and protection. A comforter is one piece of bedding made of a cloth exterior and filled with soft, synthetic fibers. The differences between duvets and comforters are that duvets have layers, require a duvet cover, and come in a variety of weights. With countless bedding options available, it's easy to get confused and difficult to know where to start. This blog provides you with a thorough look into two primary bedding options most considered by consumers. One of which is the duvet — a quilt filled with stuffing that adds comfiness, coziness, and warmth. This pillow-like filling typically consists of natural fibers like feathers, down, wool, or even synthetic alternatives, like microfiber or hollow fiber. The second choice is the comforter, a single piece of bedding that doesn’t require an outer shell or cover, like a duvet. Read on to learn everything you need to know about duvets and comforters, including their similarities and differences. Upgrade Your Sheets With Purple Purple SoftStretch® sheets are made with a soft, durable bamboo blend for maximum comfort. Shop Purple SoftStretch® Sheet Set What Is a Duvet Cover? A duvet cover is a protective layer for a duvet. It consists of two pieces of thin material sewn together with an opening at one end for inserting a duvet. They are easy to remove, store, and wash by machine. Using a duvet is easy: simply insert your duvet inside your duvet cover and seal up the open end, typically with buttons or a zipper. While it might seem like extra work compared to a blanket or comforter , this design has a purpose. A removable cover ensures the duvet stays clean, limits the need to wash the heavy duvet insert, and allows you to select an aesthetic cover of your choosing. In comparison, comforters, which are made from the same materials as a duvet insert, are not protected by a cover and require regular cleaning that oftentimes proves difficult. Duvet covers can be made from cotton, silk, bamboo fibers, flannel, or polyester. For a good night’s sleep, a breathable material is key. Our hypoallergenic PerfectStay™ Duvet Cover Set ensures optimal temperatures throughout the night by retaining heat when cool and releasing heat when warm. Benefits Considerations Soft and cozy because of inner stuffing Prone to sliding inside the duvet cover if not secured Easy to keep a duvet insert clean because an easily removable cover protects it Require a cover, often sold separately Simply change your bedding style by replacing the cover Can be a hassle to take most duvet covers off and put them on What Is a Duvet? A duvet is a plush, stuffed type of blanket that goes inside a duvet cover. Duvet inserts are sometimes called “down comforters.” Duvets, or “duvet inserts,” provide warmth, comfort, and ease of use. Unlike blankets, duvet inserts use stuffing materials like down feathers, wool, cotton, or polyester stuffing for added fluff and bulk that many sleepers find cozier. Keep in mind that stuffing materials will highly influence the price of your duvet. For example, down is generally the most expensive stuffing, but it can provide added comfort and breathability. Purple’s TempBalance™ Duvet uses a hypoallergenic down alternative. You can sleep comfortably all year round with this temperature-regulating duvet. Our quilted design keeps the duvet filling in place, so the typical annoyance of duvet movement is not a concern. What Is a Comforter? A comforter is a single piece of bedding that goes over your sheets. The typical comforter is a blanket consisting of a cloth exterior filled with soft, synthetic fibers. It typically serves as the top layer of bedding over your sheets. Available in a variety of sizes and thread counts , comforters offer ample range for creating your bedding aesthetic. Benefits Considerations You only need to buy one piece Can be hot and stuffy on warmer nights Easier to store than duvets More effort to clean Often comes in a set with matching sheets and bedding No option to change the cover if there’s a spill or stain The filling is consistently distributed for predictable coverage Differences Between Duvet and Comforter The main difference between duvets and comforters is that duvets use a cover and comforters do not. Comforters use the same materials as a duvet, but duvets are thicker than comforters. Retailers sometimes use “comforter” for “duvet” and vice versa, which can prove confusing. While duvets may require more pieces than a comforter, their design can save you time as they are easier to clean due to their removable covers. With a duvet, you simply remove the cover and wash it, whereas comforters are full of materials, so washing them can be time-consuming and problematic. Duvet Cover Size vs. Comforter Size While duvets appear fuller on your bed, they actually tend to be slightly smaller than comforters, providing a “flush” fit. In comparison, comforters are designed to hang over the sides of your bed slightly. Both duvets and comforters are available in every mattress size . Use the table below to better understand duvet and comforter standard sizes : Size Duvet Comforter Twin/Twin XL 90" x 66" 86" x 66" to 88”x 86” Full/Queen 90" x 90" 96" x 86" to 100” x 88” King/Cal King 104" x 90" 102" x 86" to 107” x 96” Sizes for duvets and comforters can vary slightly based on manufacturers. Many manufacturers size up or down from the norm by a few inches so be sure to confirm sizes per option. It’s also important to know your mattress size when selecting bedding. If you have a thicker mattress , opt for a larger duvet or comforter to ensure proper coverage around the edges. How To Choose The Right Duvet vs. Comforter There are a variety of options for duvets and comforters, which all satisfy different wants and needs. Your final choice needs to suit your particular sleeping style and preferences. Use this guide to choose the right duvet or comforter for you. 1. Material Stuffing material is a crucial factor, especially if you want to use your duvet or comforter year-round. For example, hot sleepers might prefer a down alternative as this material is more temperature-regulating, while cold sleepers might prefer down. The primary choices for duvet insert or comforter filling include: Down alternative (usually a polyester material): comfy, durable, temperature-regulating, easy to wash Down: fluffy, comfy, some are machine-washable Down and feather blend: fluffy, comfy, some are machine-washable Wool: breathable, soft, some are machine-washable Polyester: less breathable, more durable, easy to wash 2. Size To determine your blanket’s size , measure your bed. Your duvet insert or comforter should be larger than your bed’s dimensions. Manufacturers may use “queen size” to describe their duvet inserts, but it’s not always consistent between brands. First, ensure your blanket is longer and wider than your mattress. Then, consider your mattress height and how you want to style your bed. A properly sized duvet or comforter should cover the sides of your mattress without touching the floor. 3. Warmth You may have seen “fill weight” and “fill power” used to describe down or other types of filling. A fill power score indicates how fluffy a down filling is on a scale of 300-900, with 900 being the highest quality. A high number means high-quality insulation, with 600 and upwards typically denoting a high-quality option. Fill weight tells you how heavy a down filling is, but it’s less reliable for measuring warmth. You can use fill weight to find your preferred density, but fill power is better for determining the quality of a blanket’s insulation. A high-quality filling lets you enjoy a duvet or comforter year-round. Purple’s TempBalance™ Duvet uses a special temperature-regulating material for this purpose. Our down alternative provides all the comfort and convenience you need for a good night’s sleep. 4. Convenience Those who dislike the process of properly inserting a duvet into its insert may find using a comforter more convenient. However, you’ll have to use a top sheet with a comforter to avoid washing a comforter as often. Additionally, if you want to switch your comforter seasonally or for aesthetic reasons, you’ll need more storage space than you would with duvet covers. Duvet covers and inserts have a reputation for moving around, but this shouldn’t happen if you secure them. The best duvet inserts allow you to secure the duvet covers and inserts at each corner. The common options for securing duvets are: Ties Clips Loops Metal or plastic clips are easy enough to secure, but they can be bulky due to their material. Most duvets come with ties or loops, but this varies by brand. Purple’s soft-touch Velcro is the best of both worlds. Soft-touch Velcro keeps your duvet insert from moving without the need for bulky clips or fussy ties. 5. Cost Duvet inserts can cost anywhere from $50-$1,000, depending on the filling materials, fill weight, size, and brand. Pricier inserts use down, while less expensive options usually use synthetic materials, like polyester. Purple’s duvet inserts range from $229 for a twin/twin XL size to $279 for a king/California king. Every insert uses our down alternative for superior comfort at a friendlier cost. Comforters may be a bit more expensive, ranging from $30 to over $500. However, you’ll have to replace the entire item instead of just the duvet cover if it gets damaged or stained. 6. Cleaning When it comes to duvet vs. comforter care, the duvet takes top place for ease of cleaning. A duvet cover eliminates the need to wash the bulky duvet insert. The cover is easy to remove and wash making maintenance of your bedding much more effortless. By contrast, a comforter requires additional cleaning since it doesn’t have a protective cover. Getting a bulky comforter into a washing machine can be a Herculean task, most often requiring a trip to the dry cleaners. Additionally, replacing a duvet cover is much easier than replacing an entire comforter. Shop Bedding What Is the Best Duvet Insert for Hot Sleepers? The best duvet insert for hot sleepers is one filled with temperature-regulating stuffing. Down-stuffed inserts with a high fill power and low fill weight can provide comfort without trapping too much heat. Purple’s TempBalance™ Duvet is the perfect duvet insert for hot sleepers. Our easy-to-use soft-touch Velcro makes cleaning your duvet cover a breeze, and our down alternative gives you all the warm, cozy benefits of down without pokey feathers. title: Zoho alternatives: buy another CRM or build your own?
summary: Comparing Zoho alternatives? See how Airtable, Softr, monday.com, Glide, and Quickbase stack up against building a custom no-code CRM instead.
body_text: You didn't outgrow Zoho because it's a bad tool. You outgrew it because your firm's process doesn't fit neatly into anyone's template, and every workaround you've bolted on since setup has made the system a little harder to trust. So you start looking at Zoho alternatives. The problem is that most "alternatives" lists only offer you a different flavor of the same thing: another pre-built CRM with its own templates, its own pricing tiers, and its own version of the exact ceiling you just hit. There's a second option that rarely gets framed clearly: instead of buying another closed CRM, you build the one your firm actually needs on top of a no-code platform. This guide walks through both paths so you can tell which one actually solves your problem. TL;DR Zoho CRM is a capable, affordable platform, but customization, automation, and multi-user permissions get gated behind higher pricing tiers as your team grows. Off-the-shelf Zoho alternatives (other closed CRMs) fix pricing or interface complaints, but they come with the same structural limitation: you're still adapting your process to someone else's data model. No-code platforms like Airtable, Softr, monday.com, and Glide let you shape the CRM around your process instead, each with a different ceiling on permissions, client access, or workflow depth. Quickbase covers the enterprise end of that range, but it's built for IT-led teams, not a 10 to 50 person firm without a developer on staff. The real decision isn't "which CRM is best." It's "does another CRM fix what's actually broken, or is the real problem that no rigid template will ever fit." Why are service businesses looking for Zoho alternatives? Zoho CRM is priced reasonably at the entry level, and for a small team with a simple pipeline, it does the job. The friction shows up as firms grow: custom fields, advanced workflow automation, and multi-user portals live behind the Enterprise and Ultimate tiers, and pricing runs per user from roughly $14 to $52 a month depending on plan. That's a familiar shape. It's not that Zoho is uniquely restrictive, it's that any CRM built to serve thousands of different businesses has to draw its customization lines somewhere, and those lines rarely land exactly where your firm needs them. By 2025, 70% of new business applications used low-code or no-code technology, up from less than 25% in 2020, according to Gartner (2021) . A meaningful share of that shift is CRM, because customer data is exactly the kind of thing every firm structures a little differently. What's the real choice: another CRM, or a system you build yourself? Most "Zoho alternatives" content compares you to other closed CRMs: Pipedrive, HubSpot, Salesforce. Those are worth knowing about, but they solve a narrower problem than the one most operations leads are actually facing. If your complaint is "Zoho is too expensive for what we use," another CRM might fix that. If your complaint is "our process doesn't fit any CRM's default fields and stages," switching to a different closed tool usually just delays the same conversation by twelve months. No-code platforms answer a different question: instead of picking the CRM whose template happens to fit best, you define the fields, the stages, the permissions, and the automations yourself, on top of your own data. 71% of small businesses already use some form of CRM system , according to a 2024 Freshworks survey of 600 US business owners, which means most of this audience isn't choosing whether to use a CRM. They're choosing whether to keep renting someone else's structure or build their own. Here's how Zoho stacks up against the field, including the no-code route. Dimension Zoho CRM Airtable Softr monday.com Glide Quickbase Noloco Pricing model Per user, $14 to $52/mo depending on tier Per seat, plus per-editor Interface pricing Per seat Per seat, guest pricing for external users Per user, usage-based tiers Per seat, enterprise pricing Flat active-user pricing , no per-seat client fees Customization without code ⚠️ Gated by tier, deep customization needs Enterprise+ ✅ Strong on data structure ⚠️ Limited to pre-built blocks ⚠️ Board and template based ⚠️ Basic, limited backend logic ✅ Deep, but needs technical setup ✅ Full data model and workflow control Client-facing permissions ⚠️ Multi-user portals from Enterprise tier up ❌ Not built for client logins ⚠️ Page-level only ❌ Role-based only, paid guest seats ❌ Not built for client logins ✅ Yes, role-based ✅ Field and record-level permissions Where your data lives Zoho's own database Native spreadsheet-style database Connects to Airtable or Supabase Native database Connects to Airtable or Google Sheets Native, plus integrations Airtable , Noloco Tables, PostgreSQL, MySQL Best fit Simple pipeline, budget-conscious, no client access needed Teams that want structured data before adding a front end Quick client dashboards on existing Airtable data Familiar internal sales tracking Mobile-first field data, not full CRM IT-led enterprise deployments CRM, delivery, and client portal in one connected system ‍ When does building your own CRM make more sense than buying another one? Buying another CRM makes sense when your process is genuinely standard: a simple sales pipeline, a handful of stages, no client-facing access required. In that case, the fastest fix is often just picking a cheaper or simpler off-the-shelf tool. Building makes more sense once any of these are true: Your pipeline needs to connect to delivery, invoicing, or a client portal, not just sit as a standalone sales tool. Clients or external partners need to log in and see only their own records, not a shared view with everyone else's data. You've already tried two CRMs and hit the same customization ceiling both times. Your team is spending real time each week working around the tool instead of in it. That last point matters more than it sounds. A rigid CRM doesn't just annoy your team, it quietly trains them to keep a shadow spreadsheet next to it "just in case," which defeats the point of having a system of record at all. Stay on Zoho (or switch to another closed CRM) if Consider a no-code build instead if Your pipeline is simple: a handful of stages, no client access required Clients or partners need their own login showing only their records Your main complaint is price or interface, not structural fit Your CRM needs to connect directly to delivery, invoicing, or project tracking Your team hasn't hit a customization ceiling yet You've already switched CRMs once and hit the same wall again You want a system live in days with minimal setup Your team keeps a shadow spreadsheet next to the CRM to work around it You have no existing structured data to build from You're already on Airtable or Sheets and don't want to lose that data ‍ How do Airtable, Softr, monday.com, and Glide compare as Zoho alternatives? Airtable Airtable is the most common starting point for firms building their own CRM, and for good reason: linked records, custom fields, and views make it a genuinely flexible database. Many operations leads are already keeping some part of their business in an Airtable base. Where it stops being enough as a CRM on its own is client access. Airtable's sharing options are built for internal collaboration, not for giving a client a login that shows only their records. Firms that like their Airtable data usually keep it as the source of truth and add an interface layer on top rather than migrating away from it. Softr Softr turns an Airtable or Google Sheets base into a client-facing site or portal fast, which makes it a reasonable next step once Airtable alone isn't enough for client visibility. Pre-built blocks get a simple deal tracker with a client login running quickly. The tradeoff shows up as your process gets more complex. Permissions are managed page by page rather than at the data level, which gets harder to keep secure as your client list grows, and Softr pulls data live from the source on every page load, which can slow things down at scale. monday.com monday.com's CRM template is familiar and easy to sell internally, since most teams have already used its boards for project tracking. It handles an internal-only sales pipeline well. It wasn't built around external, client-facing use. Giving clients access typically means per-seat guest pricing, and permissions are role-based rather than field-level, so there's no clean way to let a client see some records but not others within the same view. Glide Glide is strong for fast, mobile-friendly apps on top of a spreadsheet or Airtable base, particularly for field teams who need a lightweight view on a phone. As a full CRM, it's a harder fit. Backend logic is limited, so multi-step workflows and more complex relational data tend to break down. It's a better match for simple record-and-view use cases than for a CRM tied into delivery and billing. Quickbase Quickbase sits at the enterprise end of this comparison: relational data, role-based permissions, and serious workflow automation, built for organizations with a dedicated IT function. For a 10 to 50 person service business without an in-house developer, that depth comes at a real cost. Implementation usually needs a consultant or technical lead, pricing is enterprise-tier, and the learning curve for non-technical operators is steep. It earns a place in this comparison because it comes up in searches, but it's rarely the right fit for this size of firm. Noloco Noloco takes a different position in this comparison: instead of a CRM template you customize within someone else's limits, it's an operating system for service businesses where your CRM, delivery tracking, and client portal all run on the same connected data. You can connect Noloco directly to an existing Airtable base, so nothing has to be re-entered, or build your data model from scratch inside Noloco. On top of that, field-level and record-level permissions mean your team and your clients can share the same system while seeing only what's relevant to them, and pricing is based on active users rather than per seat, so client access doesn't carry the same cost penalty it does with Zoho's guest-style pricing or per-seat competitors. That combination is what makes it worth considering alongside the "buy another CRM" option: instead of trading one set of limits for another, you're removing the ceiling entirely. How should you actually decide? Start by naming the specific thing that's broken. "Zoho feels expensive" and "Zoho can't model our delivery process" are different problems with different fixes, and it's worth being honest about which one you actually have before you evaluate anything. If it's genuinely a pricing or interface complaint and your process is simple, a cheaper off-the-shelf CRM may be the fastest fix. If it's a structural fit problem, no closed CRM, Zoho or otherwise, will solve it permanently. That's the signal to look at a no-code build instead. From there, match the tool to what's actually missing: Airtable if you need a better database and nothing else yet, Softr or monday.com if you need a simple client-facing layer on top of what you already have, and a connected system like Noloco if the CRM, delivery, and client access all need to work together without three separate subscriptions and a pile of Zapier automations holding them together. Final thoughts There's no universally right answer between buying another CRM and building your own. Both are legitimate paths, and the honest version of this decision depends entirely on how far off-template your actual process runs. What's worth avoiding is spending another year hopping between closed CRMs that each solve one complaint and introduce a new one. If you've already done that once, the pattern is unlikely to change the second time. Building on a flexible foundation, whether that's your existing Airtable data or a fresh system, tends to be the version of this decision that firms don't have to revisit again in twelve months. FAQ What's the main difference between a Zoho alternative and a no-code CRM? A Zoho alternative like Pipedrive or HubSpot is still a closed CRM with its own template and its own limits. A no-code CRM lets you define the fields, stages, permissions, and automations yourself, so the system follows your process instead of the other way around. Is it cheaper to switch CRMs or build one? It depends on your team size and process complexity. Switching CRMs usually has a lower upfront cost but risks hitting the same customization ceiling again. Building takes more setup time initially but tends to cost less over time once client access and automation needs grow. Can I keep my Zoho data if I move to a no-code platform? Yes, most no-code platforms support CSV import or direct integrations, and you're not required to migrate everything at once. Many firms start by exporting core records (contacts, deals) and rebuild workflows from there rather than a full one-time cutover. Do I need a developer to build my own CRM in a no-code tool? No. Platforms like Airtable, Softr, monday.com, and Noloco are built for non-technical teams using visual builders. Quickbase is the exception in this comparison; it's low-code and typically needs technical implementation support. Is Airtable a CRM on its own? Airtable can function as a basic CRM for internal pipeline tracking, but it lacks native client-facing permissions and portals. Most firms that build a CRM on Airtable add a front-end layer like Softr or Noloco on top to handle client access. What should I check before switching off Zoho? Map the specific limitation you've hit (pricing, customization, client access, automation) before comparing tools. This tells you whether another closed CRM will actually fix the problem, or whether you need a platform flexible enough to be shaped around your process instead. title: AI Gun Detection for Schools: Top Solutions & Buying Guide
summary: AI gun detection alerts school security teams in real time. Compare leading solutions, understand accuracy benchmarks, and see implementation best practices.
body_text: Traditional cameras record incidents but rarely prevent them. AI gun detection for schools is changing that equation, applying computer vision and behavioral analysis to existing camera networks so threats surface in seconds, not after the SRO radio call. For school safety directors and district security leaders weighing how to modernize campus safety without replacing infrastructure, the starting point is understanding how this technology works and which approaches actually deliver early warnings before a lockdown. This guide explains core mechanics, proven accuracy rates, five leading school-ready platforms, and a practical deployment framework. What Is AI Gun Detection for Schools? AI gun detection software transforms the cameras you already own into weapon detection systems that spot a drawn firearm and alert responders within seconds. Traditional motion or metal detectors trigger only after a shot is fired or a checkpoint is breached, but intelligent video assessment software can identify threats before violence erupts. Unlike metal detectors at the front entrance, which can feel intrusive and turn the start of the school day into an airport-style screening line, AI gun detection works invisibly through the cameras already mounted in hallways and common areas. AI gun detection software overlays computer vision on your existing camera network to spot visible firearms, verify threats, and trigger lockdown procedures in seconds. The expectation is that detection happens before the first 911 call from a classroom or front office. By automating the most challenging aspect of surveillance, AI gun detection gives School Resource Officers and local first responders critical minutes that manual monitoring routinely loses. The software operates through three escalating levels of sophistication: Basic object recognition distinguishes handgun or rifle shapes from everyday objects like phone cases, laptop bags, or umbrellas, using multi-frame analysis Contextual understanding adds spatial awareness to detect threatening situations, like a firearm in a school hallway during passing period versus a baseball bat near the athletic fields Behavioral analysis monitors body language, crowd reactions, and movement patterns for early violence indicators, from fights in the cafeteria to a student concealing an object near a restricted entry AI weapons detection technology processes live video in real time through on-premises hardware or cloud services , where machine learning analyzes every frame. When threats are detected, the system can automatically send alerts to SRO radios, administrator phones, and front-office workstations, and deliver location-tagged images to first responders within seconds. High-severity alerts are typically verified by a human analyst before campus-wide notification to prevent unnecessary lockdowns and classroom disruptions. Educational campuses present unique challenges like dense foot traffic between bells, after-school events and night games that alter lighting conditions, and open quads where students carry sports equipment, instrument cases, and theater props that can resemble weapons. Continuous learning algorithms adapt to these variables while preserving privacy by ignoring faces and other personally identifiable student information. These platforms can integrate with door controls, intercom and PA systems, mass notification tools, and other emergency communication systems, helping centralize coordination and reduce manual communication handoffs during emergencies. The result is a prevention-focused layer that transforms existing cameras from passive recording devices into proactive security assets, delivering the early-warning capability school safety teams need most. A Less Disruptive Alternative to Metal Detectors For many districts, the choice between visible screening hardware and invisible AI monitoring comes down to school climate. Metal detector lines at the front doors can create throughput delays and may signal to students that they are entering a high-security environment rather than a place of learning. They also miss anything that enters through a side door, a propped-open exit, or a parking lot. AI gun detection takes a different approach. Because it runs on cameras already installed across the campus, students never have to queue, empty backpacks, or remove jackets to walk into class. The technology stays in the background, watching for weapons and threatening behavior without interrupting the daily routine that supports learning. For parents, staff, and students, the experience feels less like a checkpoint and more like the campus they already know — only safer. Benefits of AI Gun Detection in Schools Intelligent threat detection delivers early warning that manual monitoring cannot match, alerting SROs and security operators to weapon threats while human verification prevents false lockdowns. Key advantages include: Cuts through false alarm noise : Vision Language Models (VLMs) are designed to focus on weapons and other threat-related context, which can help reduce irrelevant motion-based alerts during busy bell schedules and dismissal Provides 24/7 vigilance : Automated agents monitor every feed simultaneously across hallways, cafeterias, gyms, parking lots, and athletic fields without fatigue or shift-change vulnerabilities Enables coordinated response : When verified, location-tagged alerts flow directly to access control systems, SRO radios, and PA systems, supporting lockdown protocols and limiting attacker mobility between wings Works with existing infrastructure : Software layers onto current IP cameras from any major manufacturer with minimal capital costs and rapid deployment, preserving bond and grant dollars Student-friendly experience : Unlike metal detector checkpoints, AI gun detection operates silently in the background, avoiding the lines, bag checks, and prison-like atmosphere that can make students feel unwelcome on their own campus Maintains privacy compliance : Operates without facial recognition and minimizes video retention by focusing on threats rather than students, which can support FERPA compliance as part of broader school policies and controls Overall, the biggest benefit of integrating AI gun detection in schools is that the extra layer transforms technology from reactive incident response to proactive prevention , providing critical seconds for intervention before violence erupts in a classroom or common area. 6 AI Gun Detection Solutions for Schools District and campus security directors evaluate various vendors with different technical approaches, from behavioral analysis to walk-through screening at building entrances, based on their existing infrastructure and emergency response protocols. 1. Ambient.ai Ambient.ai reads behavioral context , which goes beyond simple object recognition and fundamentally changes how threats are detected on K-12 and higher-education campuses. While other systems only identify visible weapons, Ambient's platform can detect human behaviors that signal imminent danger. This analysis lets it detect threats even when no weapon is visible by analyzing crowd reactions, body language, and spatial context across hallways, stairwells, and exterior gathering areas. School security teams using Ambient.ai gain crucial capabilities that address the unique challenges of campus safety: Works with existing cameras : Integrates with Axis, Hikvision, Avigilon, and other systems from camera manufacturers without replacement costs, protecting prior capital investment Early warning indicators : Leveraging a library of over 150 validated threat signatures, it detects pre-incident behaviors like sudden crowd dispersal in a hallway, loitering, fights, and weapon brandishing before an incident escalates Contextual understanding : Through its AI models, it distinguishes actual threats from false positives by accounting for environmental context and behavioral analysis relevant to different campus areas Patented Access Control : Using patented technology, it correlates PACS events with corresponding video in real time, providing deeper insight into perimeter security at vestibules, side doors, and after-hours entry points Real-time investigations and forensics : Enables operators to find incident footage in an instant using everyday language to describe people, objects, or events for SRO reports and post-incident review. Human verification workflow : Automatically filters alerts, with security personnel reviewing high-severity events to prevent unnecessary lockdowns and instructional disruption Privacy-first design : Operates without facial recognition or student identification, maintaining FERPA compliance This behavioral layer provides the context that pure object detection misses, transforming existing security infrastructure into a proactive prevention system that keeps students focused on learning rather than lockdown drills. 2. ZeroEyes ZeroEyes provides AI-driven gun detection software that processes video feeds from existing security cameras. The platform uses computer vision to identify firearms in camera footage and sends alerts to school security personnel and SROs. The system focuses on object detection capabilities and integrates with standard K-12 security camera infrastructure. An important drawback of this solution is that it does not offer any detection capabilities outside of weapons, seriously limiting its ability to drive proactive prevention of fights, medical emergencies, or perimeter intrusions. 3. Scylla AI Scylla offers an edge-based video analytics solution that processes footage directly at the camera or in cloud environments. The platform provides basic weapon detection capabilities with cloud-based management for system configuration. Districts can deploy the system across existing campus camera infrastructure with standard integration protocols. 4. Omnilert Omnilert provides detection models with SOC 2 compliance for school environments. The platform offers weapon detection capabilities through existing camera systems and includes integration with mass notification and emergency communication protocols commonly used in K-12 districts. It also processes video feeds through cloud-based analytics with standard alert mechanisms. 5. VOLT AI VOLT provides a detection platform that includes weapon identification along with other security monitoring capabilities relevant to school environments. The system offers cloud-based video analysis with basic threat detection features and standard integration with existing campus camera networks. It delivers alert notifications through conventional security protocols. 6. Evolv Technologies Evolv Technologies uses physical security screening gates at building entrances for physical screening, often deployed at main entries, athletic events, and ticketed gatherings. The hardware-based approach focuses on entry point detection rather than campus-wide monitoring across hallways and exterior spaces. The system processes individuals walking through designated checkpoints and provides basic threat identification capabilities. Tips for Implementing AI Gun Detection Successful deployment builds a foundation for reliable threat detection without creating operational blind spots through camera network audit, IT infrastructure planning, alert protocol design, and continuous system tuning aligned with the school's emergency operations plan. Assess camera coverage : Map all entrances, hallways, cafeterias, gyms, and student gathering areas to verify coverage against your campus security plan. Reposition or upgrade cameras with poor resolution, backlighting from exterior windows, or blind corners near stairwells and lockers. Plan IT infrastructure : Route video feeds to the detection engine without overwhelming district network bandwidth. Design privacy policies that limit video retention and focus detection on weapons rather than student faces, in line with FERPA and district data governance. Design alert protocols : Route every detection to school security personnel or SROs for confirmation before triggering campus-wide responses. Human verification prevents unnecessary classroom disruptions and lockdowns. Maintain and tune the system : Conduct regular response drills aligned with applicable state- or district-required active threat, lockdown, or emergency exercises, track false-positive rates, and adjust detection sensitivity based on each zone's requirements, from the front vestibule to the bus loop. When cameras, software, SROs, and administrators operate as an integrated security team , automated detection becomes reliable campus protection that adapts to your school's unique lighting conditions, bell-schedule traffic patterns, and seasonal variations across athletic and after-school programming. Building Safer Schools Through Intelligent Prevention Intelligent threat detection transforms your existing cameras into active monitors, delivering alerts within seconds of weapon detection and showing operators the threat location before incidents escalate. This shifts school security from post-incident response to threat detection , without the visible barriers and screening lines that make students feel like they are entering a fortress instead of a school. Early detection systems primarily recognized movement or motion. Ambient.ai analyzes behavioral context like stance, movement patterns, and crowd reactions to identify threats even when weapons are partially concealed in a backpack or under clothing. These systems reduce false alarm rates, with human verification teams confirming genuine threats before triggering lockdown protocols that disrupt instruction. The technology integrates with your current camera networks without hardware replacement. Every entrance, hallway, cafeteria, and common area becomes a monitored space that never loses focus or requires breaks. School security teams gain critical intervention time that traditional reactive measures cannot provide. Instead of managing violence after it erupts, districts can stop threats during crucial moments before triggers are pulled. This prevention-focused approach is intended to support a secure learning environment on campus. Frequently Asked Questions How accurate is AI gun detection compared to traditional metal detectors in preventing school shootings? AI gun detection and metal detectors serve different functions. Metal detectors reliably identify metallic objects at checkpoints, but checkpoint-based screening only covers designated entry points. AI gun detection monitors continuously across entire campuses, detecting drawn weapons in real time with accuracy depending on verification workflows. Does AI gun detection software comply with FERPA and student privacy regulations if it runs on cameras that record students throughout the school day? Yes, when designed with privacy-first architecture. Compliant systems analyze video for objects and behaviors without storing biometric identifiers or using facial recognition. FERPA compliance depends in part on what data the system collects and retains, as well as how that data is maintained, used, and disclosed. What is the typical cost and timeline for deploying AI gun detection across an entire school district's existing camera network? Deployment timelines vary by district size, infrastructure, and rollout complexity, with vendors describing the process as rapid and often including a two-to-four-week parallel operations phase or a proof of concept lasting at least 30 days. Costs vary by camera count and integration complexity, structured as annual subscriptions per camera or site rather than upfront capital expenditures.

title: Partners Coffee Roasters introduces a new way to order and earn rewards with Per Diem
summary: Per Diem helps merchants grow with powerful mobile app solutions integrated seamlessly with Square.
body_text: ‍ Partners Coffee Roasters has brought its neighborhood café experience into a mobile app with help from Per Diem. The New York coffee company, which began in 2012 with a focus on great brews, community, and sustainable practices, has introduced a new ordering and loyalty app that carries its identity into the way guests order on their phones. The app is now available on the App Store and Google Play. ‍ Built with Per Diem and connected to Square point of sale, the Partners Coffee app lets guests order ahead, customize drinks, and earn rewards in a setting that feels familiar to regulars. The design and layout reflect the color, tone, and personality of the cafés so that the experience feels like Partners Coffee from the first screen to the pick-up counter. Customers can store credit, use coupons, and share referral rewards, all within a single branded space. For guests, the app turns everyday visits into a smoother routine. A regular can place a drink order on the way to the subway and find it ready when they arrive. Someone visiting a different Partners Coffee location can open the app, see the full menu, explore seasonal offerings, and start earning rewards from the first visit. Store credit and referral rewards give customers a straightforward way to keep value in their account and to invite friends into the brand. For the Partners Coffee team, the app offers a direct connection to their community without sending customers through third-party marketplaces. Orders flow into the existing Square setup, so staff see tickets in a format they already know. During busy mornings, mobile orders help spread out demand, shorten waits at the register, and give baristas more time to focus on drink quality and guest interaction. ‍ Partners Coffee has grown from a single roastery into a group of cafés that still feel closely tied to their neighborhoods. The choice to invest in a branded app reflects how guests now choose where and how to order, especially in a city where many people plan their coffee stop around a commute, a school drop off, or a meeting. With the new app, the company can offer the ease people expect while keeping the focus on its own coffee, its own spaces, and its own story. Per Diem builds mobile ordering and online ordering for cafés, bakeries, and restaurants that use Square POS. The company focuses on helping local merchants offer a clear and simple way for guests to order ahead, earn rewards, and pay online.
